text: The Patriots face a significant challenge heading into their Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday at 1 PM ET, as wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss at least four games after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and being placed on injured reserve—a blow that Mike Reiss examines in detail by breaking down which receivers will need to step up in Brown's absence and assessing how training has looked this week. Drake Maye and the offense will need to bounce back from whatever disappointment Week 1 brought, and Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's preparation in his Wednesday press conference, while the Patriots also released their full injury report ahead of the matchup. Meanwhile, in a separate matter, owner Robert Kraft made clear the organization's values by confirming he had Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows at Gillette Stadium due to what Kraft described as a "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community"—a decision that underscores the franchise's commitment to its community, something Maye himself recently demonstrated by joining his wife Ann Michael in purchasing over 50 Amazon classroom wish lists for teachers and support staff at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence.
